### 3. The three "redundant" sites and the frame floor

Each reverted alone in the worktree (`mut/m_note.py`, `m_shown.py`, `m_slots.py`, `m_conv.py`, `m_floor.py`), built, run, and restored (`git checkout`):

| Reverted | `r13a`, `r13b`, `r14c` (the review's and the fixer's controls, and four nested cases: a walked unlent callee that keeps `&caller_word`, its own local holding it, a stack word, r2) | `escfuzz14` seeds 1201 to 1203 (4,500) |
|---|---|---|
| `NoteFrameEscapeOf` lets the exact address out | no text changes | 0 flags differ |
| the "shown" stack word goes out | no text changes | 0 |
| a frame address's hand-out lets out the slots' addresses | no text changes | 0 |
| the probe's convention registers and outgoing words (H_conv) | no text changes | 1 differs (a stack-word fixture), as the fixer says it fails alone |
| the engine's frame floor (`m_floor.py`: the candidate, `setFrameFloor`, `getFrameFloor`) | no text changes (`r13a`, `r13b`, `r14*`) | 0 |

The coverage is structural. At the top level of a probe `H_conv` hands out the same set (r2, r4 to r7, every word from the call's r15 up) as the three sites do for one call, so each of the three is a subset of it. In a walked callee (`mNested`, which is tolerant too) `H_conv` does not run and the three do, and the four nested fixtures (R14-6a to 6d: a walked `c` that keeps `&caller_word` in a local and hands `&L` in r4 or r2, or the address in its outgoing stack word, to an unlent `d` that keeps it) print `return axStack_c[0];` with each site reverted; by reading, what covers them there is the walk's own rules (`handsFrame` over r0 to r7 for a caller-frame address, and the unlent call's `e.storesThrough = handed | kFrame`), which I did not instrument. The floor is redundant because with the whole-frame alias the locals stay stack locations, so the lowest left does not rise (the fixer's reading); the case that would need it is a local that vanishes from the stack space between two queries while still being reached, and I found none. No instrument row: the sites are guards, the fixture that distinguishes them would have to be one the other rule also catches.

### 4. A3-106's narrower rule, and the predicates once more

Built to defeat "unplaceable loads carry the flag, plus the slot hand-out": `hbfuzz14.py`, 4,200 fixtures (seeds 1 to 6), the pointer to the caller's word made 6 ways, laundered 12 ways (none, MACL, MACH, `mul.l`, `dmulu.l`, `mac.l` through memory, GBR, VBR, `xtrct`, the T bit, `addc`, `rotcl`/`rotcr`), sent through 19 channels, written 7 ways: **only the T-bit laundering is stale (333 of 333)**, every other cell 0 of 3,867. That is A3-95 (accepted: a frame address rebuilt from comparisons is no data flow). The cases the narrower rule could still let through need a caller-frame address that is neither made from r15 by the function (the `frame` flag) nor in a slot or register it hands out (`kOutHigh`): an address the caller passed in a register (the caller's own pointer: the caller sees it), one read from a global the caller filled (the caller escaped it), one the function builds from comparisons (A3-95). I found no fourth source.

The fail-closed predicates themselves, fixtures and fuzz:

| `ldc`/`stc` GBR and VBR as a base and as a channel; `ldc.l @r15+,gbr`; GBR-relative `mov.l r0,@(disp,gbr)`, `or.b`, `xor.b` as the walk | right (walkers `gbrmov`, `gbrrmw`, launderings `gbr`, `vbr`, `gbrl`, `vbrl`) |

### 5. What the extended fuzzer found

`escfuzz14.py` seeds 1101 to 1110 (15,000 fixtures, clean tree): 12,152 withheld, 2,848 lent; 531 texts return a register variable of a frame the escape reaches (A3-117), 88 withheld and 20 lent stale constants. Every stale constant is the T bit (A3-95) or the caller's index walks (A3-118: `idxdown` 12, `subidx` 10); no other launder, mediator or walker gives one. The 531 are all calls that show a stack argument. The old `escfuzz.py` has the same rate (seed 301: 59 of 1,500 rejected, 56 returning a register variable). Round 13's "0 wrong constants of 15,400" is right as far as it goes; the rejected texts were not counted.

Mechanisms, by reading and by the measurements (not instrumented; no temporary prints):

- **A3-117.** `ScopeLocal::markUnaliased` aliases Symbols; the call's argument words are unmapped (`markNotMapped`), so `escapeLow`'s "from there up" never names them, and A3-99 keeps the argument trial from asking the escape's alias. R14-7a (no stack argument shown) and 7f to 7i (the local above the argument words) are right; 7b to 7e (r6, r7, r6+r7, r5 to r7 set: the call shows one or two stack arguments) read the word at the call's r15 as the constant. The old fix's fixtures (R13-1a, 1b, 1c, 1d) never read that word.
- **A3-118, A3-119.** `pointerSteppedDown` follows the store's pointer through constant additions and copies; at an `INT_ADD`/`INT_SUB` with a non-constant operand it returns false. The value-set analysis catches a stride it can evaluate (R14-1a, the `shll2`, `neg`, `not` strides of R14-11), and a stride loaded from the pool or a slot or a global is a LOAD it cannot; the range is full and the guard stays from the base up. `sub r5,r2` is a step in `stepsDown` and is still missed, because the helper never reaches the join. 14 of the 20 cells of R14-14 are wrong, 6 right (the constant copy and `sub #127`, two bases each, and the `shll`-of-pool stride that does not reach the sentinel).
- **A3-122.** The cap in `stepsDown` counts the values the join's descendants produce in one pass, and the loop over the first varnode's descendants is not capped, so one pass with 4,100 stores through the pointer ends the search before the step, one hop away, is followed.

## Area 2, round 14 review

Reviewer, branch `review/2-round14-review`, on the coordinator's head `8cf615b` (patches up to 0064 in the tree). Tools, one engine pin, the ledger and this record only; no spec, engine or host file changed (every engine trial below is a scratch object linked beside the tree). New ledger rows **A2-92 to A2-100**: **two P2** (A2-92, `RuleSignMod2nOpt2`; A2-97, a printed endless loop), six P3 (A2-93 an engine failure of a whole function, A2-94 a latent `RuleThreeWayCompare`, A2-95, A2-96 and A2-98 three oracle rows, A2-99 a wrong `RuleShiftSub` in both images, masked there) and A2-100, the instrument row, closed here. **This round is not clean: two plain instruction sequences print a text that does not compute what the code computes, with no warning, so area 2's count of consecutive clean rounds stays 0.**

Patch 0064 held. Every guard was checked by value at 1, 2, 4 and 8 bytes and at the edges against a description of the machine that has no graph in it, over every constant a small width has, not over a sample (section 2): no wrong value in 25.6 million configurations at one byte, 301 million at two (the multipliers up to 2^17 and the structured list above them) and 569 million at four; the head before 0064 is wrong in 6,757, 3.05 million (of the first 132 million) and 11.8 million of the same. The guards refuse a right fold only where the product wraps its multiply and a reader cuts the wrapped bits (a hash, not a division), or in about twenty borderline sign-extension cases. The `div_product_wide` flag does not survive onto an op it does not describe, and no later rule treats a flagged product as an ordinary one (section 2.3). Both P2 defects are in code the earlier rounds had cleared **without checking it in situ**: A2-92 is in a rule the in-situ check exempted because its meaning lives in the control flow, and a checker that runs the whole function after every rule application finds it at once (section 3); A2-97 is in the structure of a function the harness could not finish (the compiled text never ends), which the harness itself could not report (A2-98).

### 2. Patch 0064 by value

**Method.** `divexh14` writes the machine out from the definition (a numerand of `xs` bytes, extended zero, signed or masked, times a constant, shifted, cut, read by five kinds of reader) and applies `RuleDivOpt` (or, in term mode, the pool of `RuleDivTermAdd` and `RuleDivTermAdd2`) to the same graph in the real engine; a rewritten graph is evaluated and compared with the definition for **every** value of the numerand. It runs the engine of the tree and, linked with `ruleaction.cc` of the head before 0064 (`73b0450`), the old one, so each configuration has two verdicts. Chunks of at most 20 minutes each, with `.done` files; the lists of constants are every multiplier up to 2^16 (1 byte) or 2^17, then the structured values above (magics of `2^k / d` and neighbours, `2^k +- 1`, sign-extended small values, all-ones runs).

| Run | Configurations | Rewritten by the tree | Wrong (tree) | Wrong (head before 0064) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RuleDivOpt`, 1-byte numerand, all 65,536 multipliers, 3 extensions | 25,559,040 | 2,949 | **0** | 6,757 (of 9,726 rewritten) |
| `RuleDivOpt`, 2 bytes, 363,663 constants | 301,112,964 | 985,805 | **0** | 3,053,476 in the first 132 million (the old object was run on 4 of the 10 chunks) |
| `RuleDivOpt`, 4 bytes, the first 400,000 of 488,247 constants | 568,800,000 | 838,057 | **0** | 11,783,564 (the last chunk on a list of 517,127 constants) |
| term mode, 1 byte | 786,432 | 76 divided | **0** | not run |
| term mode, 2 bytes | 3,633,516 | 1,541 divided | **0** | not run |
| term mode, 4 bytes | 5,026,488 | 22,582 divided | **0** | not run |

**Guards too narrow: none** (the table: no wrong value in 895 million configurations). **Guards too wide.** The same runs list what the tree refuses and the old head folded right (the old and the new object on the same list, positional comparison; the lists of constants were extended after the first two chunks, so only chunks with matching lists are used): in constants 40,000 to 79,999 of the 2-byte list 972 configurations, 3 of them with a product that fits (one degenerate fold, `x * 0x10001 >> 16` of a 16-bit x, which is `x`, a division by 1); in 80,000 to 119,999 83,629, none with a product that fits; in 120,000 to 159,999 133,118, none (132,983 of them a division by 3 or more). Everything refused with a product that fits is that one fold and about twenty sign-extension cases at the edge (1 byte, multipliers 0x101 and 0x102, where the signed product just fits). The rest is a product that wraps its multiply and is read only by readers that cut the wrapped bits (`(x16 & 0xffff) * 0x1d4c0 >> 17` cut to two bytes: a hash, which the old head turned into a division that is right for these readers), so the cost is a missed fold of a shape no division makes. The corpora's 220 `RuleDivOpt` applications print as before.

**2.3 The flag.** `PcodeOp::div_product_wide` (`addlflags` 0x4000) is set by `RuleDivTermAdd` and `RuleDivTermAdd2` on the multiply they build and never cleared; `CloneBlockOps` does not copy it (conservative: the clone is an ordinary product). Rules that could carry it onto another op were read one by one: the only way a flagged multiply is shared with an op that is not the product of a division term is common-subexpression merging with a twin multiply, and a twin needs a constant of 33 bits or more beside a 32-bit numerand, which no SH-2 code builds (`dmulu` has a 32-bit literal; the 64-bit product is a PIECE of two registers). `RuleDivOpt` reads the flag to decide that the multiply has not wrapped; no other rule reads it. The check of the flagged product in the in-situ tool (`maskwide`, 14,626 samples over the families) is the model's own, not a mask violation of the engine: the exact product is wider than the wrapped multiply's non-zero mask by design.

**The pin.** `TestDivOptExhaustiveRound14` (`Sh2DecompilerEngineTests.cpp`; 1,105,260 graphs, 5,256 rewritten, all 256 values of x, 3 s) puts the 1-byte numerand's sample in the suite: every multiplier 0 to 1,023 and every 97th above, 3 extensions, 3 forms, both shifts, every amount, 5 readers. Mutation, each mutant a reversal or a loosening of one guard of patch 0064, defined in `mutants14.py` and run against the engine test alone by `mutdrv14.py`:

| Mutant | Killed by | CHECKs |
|---|---|---|
| c: `divReadsLowBits`, an AND mask one bit wider | the new pin only | 5 |
| d: `divReadsLowBits`, a SUBPIECE one byte wider | round 13's pin only | 7 |
| b: `divProductFits` (signed), one too many | both pins | 89 |
| e: divisor limit doubled | both pins | 332 |
| f: `divProductFits` (unsigned), one too few (refuses a right fold) | the new pin through its count of rewritten graphs (5,106 < 5,200) | 1 |
| a: `divProductFits` (unsigned), one too many | lives: no wrong value in 25 million, 301 million and 569 million configurations | 0 |
| g: the mismatched pair's width test loosened | lives: no wrong value in the same runs | 0 |
| h: `divProductFits` without the numerand-wider-than-multiply test | lives: dead code (that case returns earlier) | 0 |

Round 13's own mutants 01, 02, 04 and 05 fail the new pin as before (37, 5,281, 198 and 1 CHECKs).

**Other rules of patch 0064 by value (`edge14`).** `RuleDivChain` at 1, 2, 4 and 8 bytes with every first divisor including -1: 0 wrong (the old head: 4,967 at one byte); `RuleSignForm2` at 1 and 2 bytes: 0 wrong (the old head: 1 at one byte); `RuleThreeWayCompare`: **592 wrong in 3 million seeds, all 8-byte unsigned with the constants 0 and 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF** (A2-94: the neighbour test wraps in the 64-bit `uintb`; sizes 1, 2 and 4 are clean; the old head: 20,663 wrong in 300,000). `rulefuzz14` (round 13's fuzzer with `RF_JUDGEWRAP=1`, which removes its exemption of environments where the original multiply wraps) over **6.5 million graphs** in seven modes (plain, consume masks, templates of the engine's rewrites, wide shift amounts, SH-2 shapes, wide with consume masks, depth 4): **0 wrong applications, 0 unsound masks**; the 16 seeds of round 13's replay list (`replayfix14.sh`) are right on the tree and wrong on the old head (16 of 16).

### 3. The in-situ checker: its blind spots, and a stricter one

`rulecheck13.hh` compared the value of a cone (the op's output, its readers and theirs) before and after every rule application, exempting what it could not value. Every exemption was attacked, and the checker made stricter (`rulecheck14.hh`, the same hook; `mkrc14.sh`, `relink14.sh`):

## Area 3, round 14 fix

Fixer, branch `review/3-round14-fix`, on the coordinator's head `76a43f0`. Code commits `63d40b6` to `cc83a0c` (engine patch `0066`, the host, the generator stream and oracle, the pins, the fault re-pins), then the ledger, the patch docs and this record. Own RelWithDebInfo build under the scratch directory, `-j2`, every run under `ulimit -v 4000000` with a timeout, one heavy job at a time. The container did not restart; every long run was a resumable piece.

**The rows.**

- Fixed: A3-118, A3-119 (P1); A3-117, A3-120, A3-122 (P2); A3-121 (P3, the instrument); A3-123 (routed P2, triaged to a P3 oracle false positive); A3-126 (found this round, P1).
- Open, not fixed, with a reason in the row: A3-124 (routed P1). It is not the inexact-frame-address class: its pointer is an exact constant offset from r14, which patch 0066 deliberately does not escape, and the dead stores drop even in the printed-C copy that makes no call, so there is no escape to hang the rule on. It is a subword dead-store-elimination bug on a stack struct built through a reloaded exact frame pointer -- a distinct heritage/mixed-width class that needs its own fix. Left open for a dedicated round (the status cell says so).
- The coordinator's numbering note was honoured: the one new wrong value I found is **A3-126** (A3-123 to A3-125 are the coordinator's).

### 1. The design

Since round 9, area 3's step-down detection recognised the walk below a frame address by its **form**: a constant add then a conditional step (0057), a spill (0060), an index (A3-116/0065), and the review's new non-constant strides (A3-118, A3-119). Each pattern list failed open on the next shape. This round stops recognising walks.

**Engine, patch `0066-engine-frame-escape-inexact.patch` (amends 0056 to 0065).** A frame address the stack analysis cannot place as an **exact compile-time constant offset from the frame base** now *escapes*, using 0065's whole-frame alias. `FrameEscape::classifyExact` runs over the possible frame addresses by strongly-connected component (Tarjan, iterative) and gives each one of:

- **an exact offset** -- the stack pointer's input, or a value built from one by copy, INDIRECT, addition or subtraction of a constant, PTRSUB, PTRADD of constants, or a join whose inputs all have the same exact offset;
- **"up only from an offset"** -- a value a loop carries whose every step on the loop adds a constant that is not negative, entered with exact or up values (it is at or above the loop's lowest entry, which is then aliased);
- **none** -- anything else: a register or an index added or subtracted, a stride loaded from a pool, a frame slot or a global, a join of two different offsets, a loop with a negative step or a step that is no constant, or a value whose inputs have none. A component too large to follow (4,096 members) gets none, failing closed.

An access through a member with no exact offset, or a call it is handed to, makes the frame escape; the access's own guard is widened to the whole stack space (`Heritage::widenEscapedStoreGuards`, now for LOAD guards as well as STORE guards). A3-118 (an index a loop steps), A3-119 (a register stride the value-set analysis cannot read) and A3-126 (a loop-stepped index walking up from a negative start) are all this one cause.

**The pattern detectors are demoted to precision helpers that may only add aliasing, never remove it:**

- `AliasChecker::stepsDown` takes an `atCap` argument and returns it at its 4,096-value and 65,536-op bounds, where it used to `return false` ("no walk") -- the A3-122 bug class, a cap answering "no walk" and failing open. The callers that widen an alias pass `true` (fail closed); `ActionInputPrototype`'s stack-parameter check passes `false` (a cap there keeps a parameter reference).
- `LoadGuard::pointerSteppedDown` returns `true` at its 64-hop bound.
- `reachesStepDown` is unchanged (it already failed closed at 1,024).

These still add the 0xffff-below guard where they recognise a walk, but the escape now catches whatever they miss, so no shape fails open.

**A3-117 (host, `fspec.cc`).** The words at an unlent call's r15 that the engine prints as the call's fifth and later stack arguments are unmapped (`markNotMapped`), so 0065's whole-frame alias, which aliases Symbols, never reached them: a callee that wrote one through an escaped pointer, read back after the call, printed the value stored before (`xVar2 = 1; ...; return xVar2;` for 0x55). Now `FuncCallSpecs::buildInputFromTrials` skips `markNotMapped` for a stack-argument word when a frame address of the calling function has escaped (`FrameEscape::escaped`): the word stays a mapped local the whole-frame alias covers, and the read after the call is a read of the local.

**A3-120 (host, the notes).** A frame-fact note said "is" of a word or register the host only proves *possible*. The probe now carries `Value::Sure` -- a frame address made from r15 by the function's own register operations and held there on every path, not a value a callee may have written over a slot and not a load taken for a possible frame address once the frame went out. A note says "a frame address is in ..." only when the bit it reports is `Sure`, and "a frame address may be in ..." otherwise (`kFrameEscapeNoteMay*`). R14-16e (nothing writes a frame address anywhere) now says "may"; R13-2a (the function itself stored the address in the word) keeps "is".

**A3-121 (generator, the instrument).** `GenWalk14Fn` (one seed in eight, a stream of its own) draws: loop-stepped index walks down (`@(r0,p)` with r0 counting down, `p - i`, a scaled index, the index in r0 over r14) and up from a negative start; register strides from a pool long or halfword, a frame reload or a global, added or subtracted, over a constant or an unbounded base; the stack-argument word a callee keeps and writes (A3-117's frame, r6/r7/r6r7 set so the call shows a stack argument), with the caller walking down from the kept pointer or the callee writing its own first stack-argument word; and a loop body of 4,100 to 4,300 stores through the pointer that passes the cap (A3-122). `CheckLaunderWalks` now resolves a returned temporary written exactly once with a constant, so A3-117's `return xVar2;` is compared against the run instead of being dropped as "a local" -- round 13's oracle counted such a text as a local and never read it. 44 shape kinds are pinned in `TestA365Pins`.

**A3-123 (triage, the generator oracle).** Grammar 2 seed 2616394, `n:claim-wrong:storesThrough`: function 0 byte-swaps r5's start 0x06021100 to 0x06020011 and hands it to a callee that stores a byte through it. 0x06020011 lands in r4's 4 KiB arena by chance, and the `storesThrough` arena check attributed the store to r4, which `storesThrough` does not name (the store is through r5). This is the oracle false positive of A3-100 and A3-115, in the `storesThrough` path rather than `outOrigins`; those two added a `BitwiseOfOthers` guard to `PointerRegister`, and the `storesThrough` arena check lacked it. The guard is added there; the seed is clean. P3 (an oracle false positive, no wrong engine output).

With each fix reverted, the generator alone fails seeds (section 3). The 59 fuzz fixtures the old oracle rejected unread (escfuzz.py seed 301): 56 are A3-117 (a text returning a frame register variable at a call that shows a stack argument), and 3 are the caller index walks (A3-118); `escsum14.py` counts both, and on the fixed tree there are 0 of either (section 4).

### 2. The engine's determinism

`classifyExact` first broke the allocation-failure matrix: its temporaries (the `std::map`/`std::set` keyed by `Varnode *`) were built in the pointer order of the member set, so the *sequence* of allocations in a decompile depended on where the allocator had placed each Varnode, and six fault fixtures' counts did not settle between two runs of one function (the decompiled text was identical; only the allocation order moved). It now takes the members in **creation-index order** (`Varnode::getCreateIndex`) for the component walk and emits the inexact set in that order, so the allocation sequence is reproducible. Eight area-6 fault pins then reported `MOVED` (0066 adds allocations ahead of them); each was re-pinned to the ordinal the harness printed (`fixture1` A6-10 x2 -> 84; `stack` A6-14 x6). The fault suite is 0 of 94 (section 4).

## Area 2, round 14 fix

Fixer, branch `review/2-round14-fix`, on `00aa42e`. Rows **A2-92 to A2-99 are fixed** (the two P2, A2-92 and A2-97, and the six P3); no row is accepted. **One new patch, 0067** (`0067-engine-round14-sign-mod-late-donothing-three-way-shift-sub.patch`: `ruleaction.cc` and `coreaction.cc`), pinned in the engine test and in the printed-C pins; the harness rows (A2-95, A2-96, A2-98) are test-file changes. The printed text of neither game image changes (839 and 1,554 functions, and the lent-prototype texts of the second pass: identical files). No new wrong printed value was found (one oracle regression of my own, section 3, was found by the sweeps and fixed before the commit that the rows cite). Commits: `a277e53` (engine edits and engine pins), `a1fd648` (A2-95, A2-98, printed-C pins), `0add2cb`, `867ba7c` (patch 0067, `patches/README.md`, `VENDOR.md`), `12cfca2` (A2-96 as a rewriting).

### 1. A2-92: the condition, and the siblings

The test is `lessOp->getIn(0) != base` in `RuleSignMod2nOpt2::checkMultiequalForm`, after the checks that the compare is `W s< 0`. **It is the complete condition.** The rule has five facts to establish for `V - (((W s< 0) ? V + (2^n - 1) : V) & ~(2^n - 1))`: the plain arm of the MULTIEQUAL is V (`otherBase == base`), the biased arm is `V + (2^n - 1)` of that same V (the ADD's input 0 is `base`), the join is reached from the decision block directly and through the one-in-one-out arm (`bl->getIn(1 - innerSlot) == decision`), the arm taken for `W s< 0` is the biased one (`negSlot == slot`, the flip flag included), and the final ADD adds V (`getIn(1 - slot) == base` in `applyOp`). W was the one value left free, and a different varnode that holds V's value is not a loss: after copy propagation the compare reads V itself (the same-register form still prints `param_1 % 4`, 300 functions of family 73 form 8 and the 839 and 1,554 texts show no refusal that mattered). Fixture `6043 6143 4511 8900 7103 D202 2129 3018 000B 0009 FFFF FFFC`: `mismatch` before, `agrees` after.

**Family 73 form 8** (`python3 -I tools/a2_round14/dagen14.py 3000001 300 73` through the printed-C differential): **300 of 300 agree** (270 agreed and 30 were `mismatch` on `00aa42e`).

**The sibling rules** (`RuleSignMod2nOpt`, `RuleSignMod2Opt`, `RuleSignDiv2`), read for the same missing identity: each ties the sign it reads to the value it rewrites. `RuleSignMod2nOpt` takes `a` from the sign extraction of its own shift and requires `a == vn` in the ADD (`aSlot` loop) and `a == extVn` for the shifted sign; `RuleSignMod2Opt` requires `base == otherBase`, or a SUBPIECE of the high part of it; `RuleSignDiv2` requires `a == addop->getIn(1 - i)`. Checked by construction (`TestSignModIdentityRound14`, the second part: each rule on the shape with the sign of a second register: all refuse, and all rewrite when the register is the same) and by value: `dagen14.py` family 73 form 8 now has three more variants (the sign of another register in the shapes of forms 5 to 7), 600 functions from seed 3,000,001 through the printed-C differential: 600 agree. No sibling needed a change.

### 2. A2-97 and A2-93: one root cause, in upstream's `ActionLateDoNothing`

The dump (a scratch copy of `blockaction.cc` printing the block graph before the structuring and after every rule that applied; not committed) of the 21-word fixture. The graph given to the last `CollapseStructure` (6 blocks; the earlier passes, with 12, 10, 9 and 8 blocks, are right):

```
[0] block 0 (0x06009000, bt: T != 1)        out: 2 1
[1] block 1 (0x06009004, bt: T == 1)        in: 0   out: 2 2        <- both edges to block 2
[2] block 2 (0x06009012, the loop header)   in: 0 4 1 1  out: 4 3
...
after collapseConditions:   Condition block(||) 0   in: 0   out: 2 0(back)      <- an edge to itself
after ruleBlockDoWhile:     Dowhile block 0         (the empty do { } while)
```

Block 1 is a branch whose two arms were empty blocks (`shll r0` and `add r0,r0`, dead once the constant `bf` was decided and the sum unused) that **both** were removed. The cause is in `ActionLateDoNothing::apply` (`coreaction.cc`, run just before the last structuring): it tests `removingCreatesRedundancy(bb)` (would removing this block leave a branch with both edges to one block?) for every block of the list **against the graph before any block of the list is removed**; each arm of the branch passes, because the other arm still stands between, and then both are removed. A CBRANCH with both edges to one block is what `ActionRedundBranch` removes, but it runs earlier in the main loop, never after the late removal. `CollapseStructure::collapseConditions` then merges the branch (`ruleBlockOr`: its other exit is the clause) with the branch before it into a `BlockCondition`: `BlockGraph::selfIdentify` deduplicates the identical out edges to one, and `forceOutputNum(2)` ("all conditions must have two outputs") gives the block a second out edge **to itself** (`addInEdge(this, f_loop_edge | f_back_edge)`). That self edge is structured as `do { } while (c1 || c2)`: the endless loop of A2-97. When the branch cannot be merged (the A2-93 fixture: the 4-block graph has block 1 with both edges to the exit block 3 and block 0's other exit going to block 2, which reaches 3 as well: `ruleBlockOr` finds no clause shared with the branch's exits), no rule takes the degenerate pair of edges and `selectGoto` ends in `Could not finish collapsing block structure` (status 3): **A2-93 is the same defect**, the reviewer's 'why the structurer fails was not determined' answered. The data flow was never wrong (the whole-function checker was right to find nothing): the failure is the control-flow graph after the last block removal.

The fix is in the engine (0067), in the removal: each block is tested again, live, just before it is removed (`isDoNothing()`, `removingCreatesRedundancy`, `unblockedMulti(0)`), so the second arm of a branch whose first arm has gone stays, an empty `if`, which is what any `nop` in the place of one of the instructions gave the reviewer. The fixtures: A2-97 prints `if (((in_sr & 1) != 1) && ((in_sr & 1) != 1)) { }` and then the real loop, and agrees (on the 6 inputs whose runs the emulator finishes); A2-93 prints `if ((in_sr & 1) == 1) { if (in_r0 == -0x80) { } } else { in_r1 = in_r1 + param_2; }` and agrees. The fix does not change any of the 2,393 printed texts of the images, nor the lent ones. It was **not** a matter for area 4's structuring: `blockaction.cc` is unchanged, and so is `selfIdentify`'s deduplication (upstream; the degenerate branch it was never meant to see is no longer made). A defence in `ruleBlockOr` (refuse an `orblock` whose two exits are equal) was considered and left out: it would turn the endless loop into the A2-93 failure on a graph the late removal no longer makes.

### 3. The P3 rows

* **A2-94 (`RuleThreeWayCompare`)**: `testCompareEquivalence` now refuses an unsigned pair whose smaller constant is the largest value of the width (`unsignedMax`), as the signed pair is refused at INT_MAX; only 8 bytes can wrap the 64-bit `uintb` (sizes 1, 2 and 4 cannot reach a neighbour of their own maximum). `edge14 <scratch> threeway 704 1 out` no longer reports seed 704.
* **A2-99 (`RuleShiftSub`)**: `if (c + outsize > insize) return 0;` before `c -= n/8;` is right: for a well-formed SUBPIECE it is always true (`c + outsize <= insize` is what makes the op valid), so it refuses only the ill-formed read past the top of the shifted value, whose bytes above the top are zeros while the rewritten read of V reads its bytes. It is a `no printed effect` fix, as the row said.
* **A2-95 (harness)**: the text writes `_xStack_4 = CONCAT13(...)` and reads `xStack_4`, declared `xunknown2` beside `xunknown2 xStack_2`: the high half and the low half of the write, the stack being big-endian. `StackAliasUnions` declares the wide name and every narrower local inside its bytes as members of one union (members laid out so the first bytes are the high ones on the little-endian host, a `uint8_t pad[]` before a member that is not at the end; in the C++ reading the union has a constructor, and `uint8_t` because the reading defines `char` as a class); the names are macros for the members and their declarations are removed. A name whose pieces are of no known size or not on their own alignment, and the frame mode (the names are memory of the frame there), keep the old declaration.
* **A2-96 (harness)**: the engine's reading overloaded `&&` and `||`, which evaluates both operands in C++. The text is now rewritten for that reading (`ShortCircuitOps`): every `a && b` and `a || b` of one nesting level becomes `LAND(a, b)` / `LOR(a, b)` (`||` outside `&&`, left to right, `,` `?` `:` and assignment ending an operand, parentheses, comments and constants respected), macros that evaluate the right operand only when the left does not decide and give the four-byte unsigned `Bool4` every other logical operator gives. **A first version** removed the overloads and let the built-in `&&` give a plain `bool`; that made `(a && b) - 1 >> 1` a signed `-1 >> 1` and the sweep of family 74 reported it at once (seed 3,601,817: `mismatch`, `run=7FFFFFFF pseudo=FFFFFFFF`), which is neither an engine defect nor A2-101 but an oracle regression of mine; the rewriting replaced it before any commit that the rows cite, and the function is the pin `A2-96 (arithmetic)`.
* **A2-98 (harness)**: the compiled text sets its own `RLIMIT_CPU` (`SE_GENERATED_PRINTEDC_TIMEOUT` seconds, default 30; the system headers of the guard come before the reading's own typedefs), catches `SIGXCPU`, writes `TIMEOUT` and exits 124. A batch that does not finish is run function by function as before, and a function that times out is class **`timeout`** (a finding: `IsFailing`), the rest of its batch kept. The A2-97 fixture on `00aa42e` with a 5 s limit: `timeout`, the text printed, 10 s for the batch and the single run.

### 2. Patch 0067 by value

* **`RuleSignMod2nOpt2` (A2-92).** The five facts of the form (the plain arm is V, the biased arm is `V + 2^n - 1` of the same V, the join is reached directly and through the one-in one-out arm, the biased arm is the one for `W s< 0`, the final add adds V) are all tested now; the test `lessOp->getIn(0) != base` is the last of them, and it refuses only a compare of a different varnode (a copy of V that survived copy propagation would be refused, which costs a fold and not a value). Edges: for `n` = the width minus one the mask is `0x80000000` and the SREM divisor the minimum; by hand the bias arm (`V + 0x7fffffff`, V negative) and the plain arm give `V` for every V but the minimum and 0 for the minimum, which is what `srem` by the minimum gives. Widths 1, 2 and 4 bytes are the SH-2 widths (family 73 draws every k at each, fresh seeds: 3,000 functions agree or are `narrow-c`); 8 bytes has no SH-2 route. The whole-function check over the families and the first image: 0 bad. Siblings (`RuleSignMod2nOpt`, `RuleSignMod2Opt`, `RuleSignDiv2`, `checkSignExtForm`): each ties the sign to the value it rewrites; no change needed (round 14 checked them by construction and by value; the family 73 form 8 variants agree).
* **`ActionLateDoNothing` (A2-97, A2-93).** The live test `isDoNothing && !removingCreatesRedundancy && unblockedMulti(0)` before each removal is the complete condition for the pairs: after the first of two empty arms goes, the second's input block has the edges `{outbl, arm}`, so `removingCreatesRedundancy` (all other edges lead to the arm or to `outbl`) refuses it. Read through for more than two arms: with three empty arms of nested conditionals each removal sees the graph the earlier ones left, and the last arm of every branch stays (an empty `if`). A switch's arms: `isDoNothing` refuses a switch target whose out block has several in edges (so empty arms that join are kept, the case the redundancy test cannot see), and a `BRANCHIND` block is never a do-nothing block; family 85 (jump-table switches whose arms are empty, dead or shared, 4,000 functions) agrees and recovers the switch. The infinite-loop branch is tested in the first loop only: a cycle of two empty blocks could become a one-block self loop after the first removal and be removed with its own edge; a two-block cycle cannot be built from SH-2 code (two `bra` blocks merge into one), the one-block cycle gives the engine's `Do nothing block with infinite loop` warning and a text that agrees (fixture in section 5). **Instrument check**: families 79 and 80 (random control-flow graphs with empty, nop and dead bodies, forward branches, bounded loops, a second return, entry T tested twice) were run against a scratch object of `coreaction.cc` with the live test removed: 1 `timeout` (the endless text) in the first 1,000 functions of family 79, a batch that took 78 s; on the tree 10,000 functions of 79, 10,000 of 80 and 10,000 of the empty-loop family 81 (and 40,000 of family 78, the source of A2-97) print texts that end, and every `mismatch` among them is A2-101.
* **`RuleThreeWayCompare` (A2-94).** `unsignedMax` is the mask of the compare's width, so 1, 2 and 4 byte pairs never reach it (their `offset + 1` does not wrap the 64-bit `uintb`), and 8 bytes refuse the pairs (0, 2^64 - 1) in both orders; the signed pair keeps its maximum test. The partial form (`zext + zext` with no -1, the rule subtracts 1 from the constant and refuses the -1) was not built by round 14's `edge14`: `edge15` adds it (two of five forms), 8.5 million graphs, 0 wrong, 8 percent rewritten in every form.
* **`RuleShiftSub` (A2-99).** `c + outsize > insize` is always false for a well-formed SUBPIECE, so the new line refuses only the ill-formed read; the images' applications (24 and 36) are all right under the cone check.
* **The printed-C harness.** The run guard (`RLIMIT_CPU`) works: the endless text of the scratch object is class `timeout`, the batch is split and the rest kept. `StackAliasUnions` lays the members out by the stack name's offset; no counterexample (this round's families are register-only and make no stack local; the frame fixtures of area 3 own that path). **`ShortCircuitOps`** has a defect: A2-102.

### 3. A2-101 (P2): the printer's parentheses

Found by family 79 (random control-flow graphs): two of its first 20,000 functions were `mismatch` in the printed-C differential, and family 82 was built from them. `mov r5,r1 ; bt BODY ; cmp/str r5,r4 ; bf END ; cmp/hi r6,r4 ; bf END ; BODY: add r1,r1 ; END: rts ; mov r1,r0` is printed with `... || (char)((uint4)param_2 >> 0x18) == (char)(param_1 >> 0x18) && (param_3 < param_1)` where the engine's tree is `(b0 || b1 || b2 || b3) && (param_3 < param_1)`: the `||` of the four byte compares is the first operand of an `&&`, printed without parentheses, so C reads `b0 || b1 || b2 || (b3 && c)`. The cause is the pair of conditions in `printc.cc`: `opCbranch` opens a parenthesis around a condition only when `comma_separate` is not set (`yesparen = !isSet(comma_separate)`), and `emitBlockCondition` sets `comma_separate` for everything it emits once it is nested as the second operand of another block condition (the first operand of the inner `&&` inherits it); a first operand that is a `BOOL_OR` then has no parentheses and no operator of the `&&` above it to hide behind. Upstream's own comment in the function: `FIXME: get rid of parens and properly emit && and ||`. The carry of `addc`/`subc` and the overflow of `addv`/`subv`/`negc` are such `||`s (and the sum is a statement, so the first operand is printed `S, A || B` in comma form), so the multiword idioms are hit as much as the string scan: 377 of 3,000 functions of family 82 (6 to 14 per 200, whichever carry instruction), 94 of 21,000 under the in-situ run, 2 of 20,000 of families 79 and 80. Without the leading `bt` the text is `(A || B) && c` and agrees; with it the shape needs the outer `||` above the inner `&&`.

**Scratch fix**, two variants as scratch objects of `printc.cc` (relinked into the generated-tests and the corpus programs; not committed). The narrow one parenthesizes the first operand of a comma-mode `&&` only when it is a `t_copy` block whose last op is an unflipped CBRANCH that reads an implied `BOOL_OR`: all three fixtures of the row agree; family 82 (3,000 functions), families 79 and 80 (10,000 each, the seeds of the two finds) 0 `mismatch`, and the loop forms of family 82 (a loop condition made of the same operands) agree with and without it. The wide one parenthesizes every first operand in comma mode (simpler, rightness by construction) and changes 17 texts of the first image and 34 of the second by parentheses alone. **Corpus**: the stock engine, the narrow fix and the wide fix on both images (`SE_GAME_OUT`): stock against narrow 0 and 0 files differ, so no function of the two images has the defect; stock against wide 17 and 34 differ, every one a redundant pair of parentheses (the ones I read: `(('\x01' < param_1) && ...)`, `((cVar7 = SMPC_SR, ...) && ...)`).

### 3. A2-101: patch 0069

`PrintC::emitBlockCondition` gives the second operand of a nested `&&`/`||` its own parentheses and not the first; `opCbranch` opens none in comma mode. The fix is the review's wide variant: the first operand is parenthesized whenever the condition is nested (`comma_separate` set on entry), so no operator of the first block can bind looser than the `&&` or `||` it is under, whatever it is (an `||`, a comma, a ternary). The cost is redundant parentheses where the first operand is a single comparison (the review counted 17 and 34 texts of the two images). Pins: `A2-101 #0` to `#2` in the printed-C differential (the review's three fixtures; `mismatch` without the patch, the review's run on `215d303`), and `A2-120`, `A2-121` (`narrow-c`).

* The draw-order fix was found by comparing draw traces of 15 seeds and the default and printed-C runs; a draw site that neither reaches could still differ between compilers.

#### Coordinator: the CI repair, part 2 (patch 0070, the web front end, Windows waits)

* **UBSan.** With the sanitizer job linking again, it reported undefined shifts outside the two accepted SLEIGH sites, reached by rounds 9 to 15: `sign_extend` (`address.cc:1002`, a negative value shifted left; `:1003`, a negative count where sizeout is below sizein), `PcodeOp::getConsumeLocal` (`op.cc:890-891`, `PIECE` with a low input as wide as the output; `op.cc:944`, `INT_LEFT` by 64 or more, up to 65,536), and two lines of the engine tests' 64-bit model given 16-byte values. Patch 0070 defines each with the result x86 gave (the shift done unsigned, a count taken modulo 64), except the `PIECE` case: there x86 made the low input consume nothing (`outc ^ (outc << 0)`), which is the direction that can remove live code, and it now consumes every output bit. CI's own scripts on a local ASan + UBSan Debug build (`run-decompiler-sanitizers.sh`, `check-sanitizer-logs.sh`): passed, no report beyond the two accepted sites.
* **The web front end** had not compiled since 13 October: `App.cpp` used `mSourceSerial`, `LiveHas` and `mPatchLib` unconditionally while `App.h` declared them under `SE_ENABLE_LIVE`. The first two are declared outside it (`LiveHas` has a non-live body already); the patch count is read under it. Every front-end source that does not include SDL2 passes `em++ -fsyntax-only` with the web build's flags (53 files; the 4 SDL2 ones need the port, which this container cannot download).
* **Windows Debug**: a panel test waited 30 s for the large fixture's `TooLarge`; the decompiler tests' waits are `dts::kWaitMs`, ten times as long without `NDEBUG`.
* Matrix on `3427689` (master `d2ae3dd` with patch 0070): build ok; ctest 97 of 97 and 6 of 6 Live; fault matrix 0 of 94; generator 0 failing (3,000, 1,000, 20,000) and printed C 0 mismatch; `VENDOR_EXIT 0`, empty diff; both images unchanged from the baseline (839 and 1,554 ok, 0 dropped, missing and said 0 and 4, lending 678 (956) and 1,038 (1,310), real entries 474 (645) and 724 (975)).

## A3-124 fix

Fixer, branch `review/3-a3124-fix`, on `f3c13b0`. Engine patch `0068-engine-deadcode-late-stack-reads.patch` (0067 is area 2's; master's 0069 and 0070 came after the base, and 0068 touches neither `printc.cc`, `address.cc` nor `op.cc`, only `op.hh`). Own RelWithDebInfo build under the scratch directory, `-j2`, every test binary under `ulimit -v 4000000` with a timeout, one heavy job at a time, runs split into pieces of 20 minutes or less with a `.done` per piece.

**The rows.**

- Fixed: A3-124 (P1, the row).
- Found and fixed: A3-127 (P1: upstream's INDIRECT collapse built a 5-byte piece for a 4-byte local; the corpus function's own cause, and 12 more `-O0` struct builders in each save state), A3-128 (P1: a call's guard lost its force before a STORE through a reloaded pointer was folded; hwram008 060554B6), A3-129 (P1, the instrument: the conservation ledger took every frame fold for conserved). A3-125 is reserved and A3-126 was area 3's; the numbering starts at A3-127 as asked.

### 1. The cause

**Shrunk.** Fourteen words drop a store with no call and no frame pointer (`TestA3124Fix` pin A):

```
add #-24,r15 ; mov r15,r1 ; add #12,r1 ; mov.l r1,@(20,r15)     ; the slot holds &S
mov.l @(20,r15),r1 ; mov #-1,r2 ; mov.l r2,@r1                  ; S = 0xFFFFFFFF
mov.l @(20,r15),r1 ; add #1,r1 ; mov.b r5,@r1                   ; S.b[1] = r5
mov.l @(20,r15),r1 ; mov.l @r1,r0 ; rts ; add #24,r15           ; return S
```

The head printed `Stack_b = CONCAT12(param_2,Stack_b._1_2_); return Stack_b;` (an `unkbyte3` read of three bytes of the frame's input), a mismatch on the run. Kept in a register instead of the slot (pin G), the same stores were always right. A trace of every action, rule and heritage range (a temporary, environment-gated build, not committed) gave the sequence:

1. Pass 0 folds the slot's store and its three reloads into stack Varnodes (`RuleStoreVarnode`, `RuleLoadVarnode`).
2. Pass 1 heritages the slot. The word STORE is unmodeled (its pointer is a frame-slot read, 0061), so it and the byte STORE carry INDIRECT guards on the slot; the first reload resolves to `sp-12` at once, the second only once the word STORE's guard collapses (it is folded in the same rule pass), the third only once the byte STORE's guard collapses: **each STORE whose guard covers the slot costs the reload after it one more pass**.
3. Heritage pass 2 links `sp-12` with the word store as its only access (reads 0). Dead code is allowed in the stack space after heritage pass 1 (`deadcodedelay` 1): the word store's COPY, and the INDIRECT the byte STORE had put on `sp-12`, have no reader and are removed.
4. The byte STORE and the final LOAD are folded; heritage pass 3 finds the LOAD's read in a range linked before, after dead code ran in the space: upstream's check (`Heritage::heritage`, "Heritage AFTER dead removal") bumps the dead code delay and restarts. But `bumpDeadcodeDelay` raised it **once, by one pass** (to 2): the restarted run allowed dead code after heritage pass 2 and removed the store again, the read was linked in pass 3 again, and the second detection did nothing (an override was installed, and the restart group allows one restart). The read was linked to the frame's input.

So the dead-store elimination is not wrong in itself: dead code ran in the stack space before every read of the stack had been found, and upstream's remedy for exactly that was bounded too low. The row's printed-C copy (pin F, eight byte stores through the reload) needs as many passes as it has stores.

**The corpus function is a second engine bug (ledger A3-127).** With the dead code fix alone reverted (mutant `E_bump`), hwram007 060228B4 and hwram008 06061D90 are right; with the second fix alone reverted (`E_front`) the head's text comes back, 2 of 8 byte stores. `Funcdata::opCollapseIndirectsForCopy` (upstream's, `funcdata_op.cc`) turns the INDIRECT a STORE put on a wider local into pieces when the STORE becomes a COPY. For a COPY in the middle of the local (bytes before and after it), the front piece was made `bytesAfter` long instead of `bytesBefore`: a byte stored at offset 1 of a word (1 before, 2 after) or 2 (2 before, 1 after) built a 5-byte PIECE for a 4-byte local, `SUB42(x,3)` reading past its input. Pin C shows it alone: a word -1 stored and read directly, a byte through the reloaded pointer; the head printed `axStack_c._0_2_ = 0xff; axStack_c[2] = param_2; axStack_c._3_2_ = 0xffff;`, the byte a byte late. In the `-O0` copy every word gets bytes at offsets 1 and 2, the malformed pieces were simplified away, and six stores went with them.

**One more way of the same class, found by the ledger once it counted (section 3).**

- A call that may read a local of an escaped frame keeps the store before it through the address force on its INDIRECT (`guardCalls`' `holdind`, kept by `ActionDeadCode` only for a direct write). Both conditions are decided too early for a STORE through a reloaded pointer: the scope may not call the range address-tied yet when the guard is made, and the value is a direct write only once the STORE folds, by which time `ActionDeadCode` had cleared the force for good. hwram008 060554B6 stores 0 at `S+4` through the slot's pointer (`mov.l r2,@(4,r7)`), calls three functions that may read S (the frame escaped), then writes `S+4` again: the head dropped `xStack_3c = 0`. Ledger A3-128.

### 2. The fix: engine patch `0068-engine-deadcode-late-stack-reads.patch`

The rule held: a STORE is removed only once every access that may read a byte of it has been found and linked. In the engine that is "dead code does not run in a space before every read of it has been found", and Ghidra's own remedy for a read found late (raise the dead code delay, restart) is made complete instead of replaced:

- **The delay is raised past the pass that found the read** (`Heritage::bumpDeadcodeDelay`): to that pass when it is beyond the delay in force (or one more), and again whenever a later generation finds a read later still. The raises of one generation are one restart (the latest pass any of them asked for); after three restarts the delay is set so that dead code never runs in the space (`noDeadcodeDelay`): the writes stay, the text is longer, nothing is lost. The upstream early returns (an override installed, a global delay) are gone. `ActionRestartGroup` allows one more restart per raise (`Override::numDeadcodeBumps`).
- **A STORE folded late into a range heritaged before needs no check of its own.** An earlier draft raised the delay for such a write too (a COPY `RuleStoreVarnode` made, with no reader, in a range linked before). It was dropped: dead code removes the guard the STORE put on the range only when nothing read it, so a read of the range after the store either does not exist (the write is dead in fact) or was found late itself, and that read raises the delay already. Without it the pins, the generator matrix and the corpora find no loss (sections 5 to 7).
- **A call's INDIRECT on a local of an escaped frame keeps its address force** (`guardCalls` sets it once `FrameEscape` found an escape; `ActionDeadCode::callMayReadFrame` keeps it when the value is not a direct write yet). A3-128. Not for the save of a callee-saved register (`ActionDeadCode::isSavePush`: the local's word, back through the guards and the joins of paths before it, was written by a push -- `mov.l Rm,@-r15` for r8 to r14, `sts.l`/`stc.l` of MACH, MACL, PR, SR, GBR or VBR to `@-r15`, the frame ledger's own list -- of that register's whole entry value; half of MACL stored with `mov.w` is data, pin N, grammar 2 seed 10032, and so is GBR's word stored with `mov.l r2,@(12,r14)`, pin P, seed 11612): no callee is handed the save area (the frame ledger's own rule), and a first version that held every push printed them as local writes (`xStack_4 = unaff_r8;`) and cost hwram007 two lent signatures (060322D4, 06032490: "it reads r8 on entry"); pins M to P hold it (O: the call in a loop, the save reaching its guard through the loop's join, as in hwram007 0600894A).
- **The INDIRECT collapse's front piece is `bytesBefore` long** (`opCollapseIndirectsForCopy`). A3-127; the bug is upstream's (not filed upstream from here).

The fix is not a shape: it does not look for a pointer kept in a frame slot. A read through any pointer the analysis resolves late (a slot, a chain of guarded stores, a join that settles late) delays dead code until it is linked, and the bound fails closed.

**Cost.** A function with a late read was restarted once before and may now be restarted up to four times; the restarts are where the warning "Restarted to delay deadcode elimination for space: stack" already stood. The "Heritage AFTER dead removal" header the head printed on such functions is gone from their final text, since the last generation finds nothing late: two fixtures carried it at the head (`r12o.src`, `r13b.src`, section 7) and carry it no more; the corpora had none, and their restarted functions (2 and 12) are the same at both.

### 3. Why the ledger missed it, and the frame ledger

**Why.** The conservation oracle pairs each access of the reference run (the same request with every address volatile) with what the shown run did with it. The frame is no memory the request can mark volatile: in **both** runs a LOAD or STORE through a frame address is folded into a stack Varnode, a variable, so the reference run's list never holds it; and the shown run's record of the fold (`fate_folded_ordinary`, `frame` set) pairs with nothing and was taken for conservation. What happened to the variable write after the fold was recorded nowhere: patch 0017 records a destroyed op only while it is still a LOAD, STORE or volatile access, and the COPY a STORE becomes is none. `DeadIsLoss` skips frame records too. So "0 accesses dropped against the reference run" was true and said nothing about the frame: A3-124's stores were folded, then removed, and both runs agreed. The step 5 note ("four of six byte reads ended dead") was the same function seen from its reads.

**The frame ledger** (`FrontEnd/tests/FrameLedger.h`, `dts::FrameLosses`, from patch 0068's records), in `ReferenceOk`, `TestGameCode` (its own count, "frame writes lost", and a CHECK) and the generator (a finding, `frame-lost`):

- The engine records how a frame fold ends a second time: `fate_frame_unread` when the COPY is destroyed and its value was never *forwarded* (a reader that stays given it in another form: propagation, a rule finding it equal to something or folding it into a constant, a `totalReplace`; walked back through any op, 64 at most; an op whose readers all died as dead never forwarded its value), `fate_frame_removed` when it goes with an unreachable block. A PIECE or SUBPIECE whose sizes do not add up is recorded too (`fate_malformed_piece`): what flows through it is no value the code computed, so no record of the accesses in it can be trusted (A3-127's 5-byte pieces).
- The host turns them into `AccessFate::FrameUnread`, `FrameRemoved`, `MalformedPiece` (with the flow position of each), and `DecompileResult::frameCalls`: the calls heritage guarded a stack local at (their effect on it is unknown; a lent callee's is known), with the local, unless it lies wholly below the stack pointer the callee is entered with.
- Three refinements, each a false loss the generator matrix found on the fixed tree (the text right) and each pinned (`TestA3124Fix` J to L): a frame read destroyed with its value forwarded passes the mark on to what it read (grammar 2 seed 572: a pop forwarded into `r1 & 0`, a constant, before the stack was linked to its push); a frame read whose value is forwarded notes the STOREs whose guards it read through (the chain of INDIRECTs, each guarding a STORE whose pointer was still unresolved, back from the read's input), and each is marked read when it is folded into the bytes read (`Funcdata::noteGuardRead`; frame124 seed 2595: a halfword read twice and xored with itself while the word store under it still went through the reloaded pointer, the store folded after its readers went). Only that chain and those bytes. The first version marked a STORE through any guard any walk passed; the mutation table caught it twice: every reload of A3-124's pointer reads the slot through the guards of the STOREs before it, so with the delay's raise reverted the ledger found none of the 14 losses in the pins, and A3-128's store was marked through the guard of the call after it, so with the call fix reverted pin I's loss went unseen; and a call's guard that `RuleAliasUpdate` later removes, because no pointer to the local reaches the call, takes the call's record with it (`Funcdata::dropFrameCall`; grammar 2 seeds 996, 2191, 4666, 19596).
- `FrameLosses` decides, byte by byte over the flow's blocks as first followed: a write that went unread is a loss when some path from it reaches a byte read before folded writes of the frame have covered it. A read is a folded read of the frame whose own value something used (a pop of a register the engine takes for unaffected is no use), or a guarded call over the bytes, but for the save of a callee-saved register (a push of r8 to r14, `sts.l`/`stc.l` to `@-r15`), which no callee is handed. Only folded writes (frame offsets the engine placed) cover a byte. A malformed piece is counted apart ("malformed pieces"); both counts must be 0.

What it does not see: a value forwarded in an equal form to a reader that dies later counts as used (the walk back marks every fold the value was made from: it can hide a loss, never invent one), and a store kept but read back wrong is a value error for the value oracles (the printed-C differential, the pins), not an access lost.

**What it counts with each fix reverted** (section 6): with the delay's raise reverted, 14 frame losses in the pins' lines and 31 frame-lost seeds in 300; with the collapse reverted, 47 malformed pieces in each save state (060228B4's eight among them) and 28 malformed-piece seeds; with the call guard's force reverted, pin I's loss, 1 frame write lost in hwram008 (060554B6) and 2 frame-lost seeds in 3,000. On the fixed tree: 0 and 0 in both save states.

### 4. The generator: the frame124 stream

`GenFrame124Fn` (`Sh2GeneratedTests.cpp`, one seed in four, a stream of its own) draws the class: a frame of 32 bytes on r15 or, `-O0` style, on r14 (pushed, r15 copied); an 8-byte struct S at frame + 8, 12 or 16; &S in the slot at frame + 28. S is filled whole first (two words of constants, or eight byte stores in a random order), then 1 to 8 byte, halfword and word stores at aligned offsets (r4 to r7, or a constant), each through the pointer reloaded from the slot (one in five through the previous store's r1); then 1 to 3 reads of S, byte, halfword or word wide (wider or narrower than the stores), through the reloaded pointer or directly at S's frame offset, added or xored into r0. Some hand &S to a callee between the stores and the reads: a lent `rts ; nop` (`call`), or a withheld one that reads a word of S through r4 (`callr`, A3-128's shape: the caller writes that word again after the call, so only the call reads the store before it). Shapes `frame124.<r15|r14>.<words|bytes>.<nocall|call|callr>.<b|w|l|mixed>`, 32 kinds, each pinned to be drawn (`TestA365Pins`, "frame124 draws"; the bytes fill has no call). Each draw is a statement of its own (the generator's rule for an order GCC and Clang agree on).

- A function without a call goes through the printed-C differential with the rest (its text compiled and run beside the code for every input): a value the text lost is a `mismatch`.
- Every one, with a call or not, goes through the frame ledger (`CheckFrame124Ledger`: the callee decompiled and lent first): a frame write lost or a malformed piece is a finding (`frame-lost`, `malformed-piece`). A text with a call reads S through the kept pointer after it (the frame escaped), which no constant check resolves; the ledger is its check.
- The grammar 1 and 2 functions (`TestGenerated`) go through the frame ledger too, beside the trace-based ledger.

`SE_GENERATED_PRINTEDC_FRAME124=0` leaves the stream out; `SE_GENERATED_FRAME124_WORDS` replays one function through the ledger, `SE_GENERATED_PRINTEDC_WORDS` through the differential. A `frame124_` function the differential skips (a text that takes a local's address) is counted, not failed; in printed-C seeds 1 to 3,000 the stream drew 786 functions, 521 without a call: 518 compared, 3 skipped.

The printed-C harness learned one thing for this stream: a name the engine makes for a write wider than the symbol it starts at (`_xStack_14 = CONCAT31(...)` over the two-byte `xStack_14` and `xStack_12`) is a separate variable in the harness's C, so a later read of `xStack_12` read nothing (frame124 seeds 1529, 1651, 2229: mismatches of right texts). After each such write the harness now gives every declared local inside it its bytes, the machine's order (`Sh2GeneratedTests.cpp`, the underscore-name block; a printed-C pin, `A3-124 _xStack_14 over xStack_12`).

`TestA3124Fix` (`Sh2DecompilerTests.cpp`), each function at 06009000, each text checked for a fragment (pins J to L are the ledger's own false losses, texts that are right), for no "Heritage AFTER dead removal" or "Exceeded maximum restarts", for an empty frame ledger and `ReferenceOk` (which runs the ledger and the malformed-piece count), and, where PseudoEval reads it, evaluated against the code on the emulator for three inputs:

The ledger itself, on made-up records: a write that went unread and is read in the next block is a loss; covered whole first by a folded write, or read only by an access removed with unreachable code, or by a read whose value nothing used, it is not; another byte covered leaves the loss; a call the engine guarded a local at reads it, but not a callee-saved register's push (`mov.l r14,@-r15`), and a stack argument's push (`mov.l r4,@-r15`) is read.

`TestEngineEdgePaths`' "restart limit alone" fixture (a pointer to a slot spilled and reloaded, a global whose first store was dead, found two passes late) was the restart limit's only end-to-end pin: it now restarts twice and prints `xRam06070000 = param_2; return param_2;`, right, and is pinned so; the limit itself stays pinned end to end by the truncated switch (`TestFlowUncertainty`) and its warning's classification.

### 10. Limits

- **The frame ledger's forwarding is an approximation.** A value forwarded in another form marks every fold it was made from (walked back through any op, 64 at most): the walk can hide a loss, never invent one. Three false losses came from where the marks did not reach (a read forwarded before the stack was linked, a read through a STORE's guard, a call guard the alias analysis removed); each is fixed and pinned (J to L). A write destroyed by dead code before a marked reader of it could still be reported; the matrix and both corpora show none.
- **The save rule is the SH-2's.** `isSavePush` reads the instruction word for the push forms; a callee that read its caller's save area through an escaped frame address would see a save the text dropped; none of the fixtures, generator seeds or corpus functions read here does. The frame ledger exempts the same pushes, so the two agree.
- **Jumptable recovery takes no restart** (upstream's `ActionRestartGroup` returns at once during it): a read found late inside a jumptable's recovery is not restarted there; the function's own decompile has its own raises. No fixture reaches it.
- **Kept though no test fails without them:** `E_hold` (the hold when the guard is made; `E_keep` alone covers the pins and corpora), `E_never` (the fail-closed delay after three raises; nothing raises three times), `E_wide` (whole words only; the push test implies it).
- **More text where a frame escapes.** Stores before a call that may read the frame are printed (06019A56, 06027420's lending text); some locals the head folded into arrays are separate symbols. No lent signature changed.
- **Mutation rows.** All but the call guard's were measured on `e20866e`, whose engine differs from the final one only in the save rule (section 6).
- **A3-127 is upstream's bug**; it is not filed upstream from here.

### 1. The tools

`Docs/Decompiler/tools/a3_round15/`, on the round 11 to 14 driver (`bdrv.sh`, `run.sh`, `mk.py`, `asm.py`, `drvmain.inc` rebuilt from the suite's own source; `drvmain.inc` now also runs `ReferenceOk` after the entry and prints `LEDGER ok` or `LEDGER BAD` with the conservation lines, so the frame ledger judges every fixture, `NOLEDGER=1` leaves it out):

- `frame15.py SEED COUNT`: frame-struct fixtures beyond the frame124 stream. A 16-byte struct S in a 48-byte frame, `&S` kept behind a chain of 1 to 3 pointer slots (`F15_LEVELS`), 1 to 24 byte, halfword and word stores at any legal offset through the reloaded pointer or direct (`F15_NST`), an optional call handed the reloaded pointer (`F15_CALL`: none, lent, unlent), 1 to 3 reads of any width, and a fill (`F15_FILL`: words, bytes, halves, none, **save** = the entry values of r8 to r14 stored whole, **cover** = S tiled exactly by random stores with no earlier fill). `f15run.sh` and `f15sum.py` run the driver and count `LEDGER BAD` and oracle mismatches; `f15pc.py` runs each call-free fixture through the generator's printed-C differential (`SE_GENERATED_PRINTEDC_WORDS`: the text compiled and run beside the code: the value oracle for texts PseudoEval cannot read), and `shrink15.py` delta-debugs one by dropping store groups.
- `r15a.src` to `r15r.src`: about 90 hand fixtures (the push forms of section 3, the pointer chains, the save-slot variants, the uninitialised-word variants, the cap blinding of section 4; A3-136's call removed with its block is the generator's replay line).
- `matrix15.sh`, `hidden15.sh`, `gen_range.sh`: the ranges of section 7; `mkrows15.py`: the rows of this round (their eight cells are checked there); `dbg_engine.diff`: the temporary prints (never applied to the tree): `SE_DBG_BUMP` (every dead code delay raise, the dead code in the stack space with the ops it kills, the guards made for each STORE, the INDIRECTs `opDestroy` removes with a backtrace, each alias collapse), `SE_DBG_RAW` (`printRaw` after each heritage pass), `SE_DBG_CAP` (where the ledger's walk reaches its 64-op cap).

### 2. 0068's dead code delay

The delay is raised in `Heritage::bumpDeadcodeDelay`, which is called from two places only: `removeRevisitedMarkers` and the loop in `Heritage::heritage` that finds a **free read** (a Varnode read, not written) in a range heritaged before, after dead code removed something in the space. So the delay protects against one thing: a read that arrives late. A write that arrives late is protected by the INDIRECT guard the engine puts on the range for a STORE it cannot yet place; the A3-124 fix's own argument ("a STORE folded late into a range heritaged before needs no check of its own") rests on that guard staying until the STORE is folded.

The attack was therefore a STORE whose guard does not stay. Two ways were found, both with no call and a direct read of the bytes (A3-130, A3-132); each is the shape of the A3-124 fixture with one more step of indirection, and each prints one "Restarted to delay deadcode elimination for space: stack" warning (A3-130) or none (A3-132) and still loses the store:

- **A3-130, a pointer reached by two frame slots** (R15-7a): the guards are made at heritage pass 1 and destroyed in the same pass by `Heritage::reprocessFreeStores`, which unmarks the STORE once the stack is linked because the second reload is a LOAD through a now-modeled frame address, and `FrameEscape::compute` has `case CPUI_LOAD: continue` ("what it reads is memory"). The LOAD is folded into a stack read a pass later, the STORE after it, and the COPY it makes has no reader: the direct read of the word was linked to the older write at pass 1. With the delay raised to the pass that found the read (the bump at pass 2) dead code still removed it, as no read is found late. One slot (R15-7b), a call handed a frame address (8a, 8c), the frame address published in a global (8b) are right: the frame escapes, and every STORE through a pointer loaded from memory is guarded (0063). Three levels fail the same way (R15-7c).
- **A3-132, the save slot** (R15-5a): a COPY of an unaffected register's entry value to a frame word makes the word "not mapped" (`ActionRestrictLocal`), the alias analysis then says it has no local alias and `opCollapseIndirectsForAlias` destroys the STORE's guard on it at pass 1 (`noalias=1`, `guard=0` in the trace). 0063 kept the slots an indexed STORE may write (`isGuarded` of a valid STORE guard); a pointer reloaded from a frame slot has no such guard.

**Does "fails closed" mean no stack store is removed?** By reading: the fourth raise sets `noDeadcodeDelay` (0x10000), `HeritageInfo::deadcodedelay` is read by `deadRemovalAllowed` only, `ActionDeadCode` skips the space and marks every stack Varnode consumed; `ActionRestartGroup` allows `maxrestarts + numDeadcodeBumps` restarts, so the fourth restart is taken. I did not find a function that reaches the fourth raise: `frame15.py` with an escape (a call handed the reloaded pointer) and 1, 2 and 3 slots, 24 stores, words, bytes and halves, lent and unlent callee: **500 fixtures, 0 `LEDGER BAD`, 1 oracle mismatch which is PseudoEval reading an array (`return axStack_24`)**. Without an escape the chains are lost by the guard, not by the delay (A3-130), and a function that the delay does reach three times needs more late reads than I could draw. The terminal state itself (which would show as many stack writes in the text) was therefore not observed; `E_never` stays a bound with no fixture, as the A3-124 record says. This is a limit of the review, not a finding.

### 3. isSavePush

`ActionDeadCode::isSavePush` reads the instruction word at the COPY's address (`mov.l Rm,@-r15` for r8 to r14, `sts.l`/`stc.l` of MACH, MACL, PR, SR, GBR, VBR) and takes a call's INDIRECT on a local as no read of the frame only when every write the guards and joins lead back to is such a push of the register's whole entry value. Built to defeat it (`r15a.src`, base and head side by side, `r15f.src`, `r15e.src`):

| Fixture | Result |
|---|---|
| R15-1a, 1b: push r8, the push slot's address handed to a lent callee that reads it (in r4; published in a global) | lent `f(void)` returning the callee's read, which is the caller's r8; **same on f3c13b0** (A3-135, P3: the push is no read for the lending trials either) |
| R15-1c: r8 pushed as the fifth stack argument of a callee that reads it | withheld ("it calls 0x06009100, whose signature is not known"), right |
| R15-1d, 1e: push r8, overwritten by a data store through the reloaded pointer, the slot's address handed to a callee, the slot read after | `return unaff_r8;` where the code returns r5: **the same on the base, and the same with a push through r1 that `isSavePush` does not accept (R15-1e2)**: the cause is A3-132, not the exemption |
| R15-1f: push r8, overwritten by a direct data store through a register copy of r15, handed to a callee | right (lent `f(int)`) |
| R15-3a to 3g: the same slot first written by a constant, an argument, r8 (push and plain store), after the allocation or by a push | right except r8 (A3-132), which also holds for r9, r14, GBR, VBR (R15-5a to 5k) and not for MACL, a halfword or byte of r8, or r8 + 1 |
| R15-4a to 4f | 4a, 4b, 4f (no call, a call not handed the frame, a lent callee) are A3-132; 4c to 4e right |

No store was dropped because of the exemption itself: the cases it exempts are exactly the cases the lending trials already exempted, and the two that are wrong are wrong on the base.

### 4. The frame ledger's blind spot

"The walk back from a forwarded value can hide a loss but never invent one": it can hide a loss in two ways, one is the cap. `noteFrameFoldForwarded` stops after 64 ops and then takes every fold of the function as forwarded (`frameFoldsAllRead`), and 4,096 guard records do the same. A3-130's function with a long expression on the result (R15-15a to 15d: 0, 10, 40, 80 xor/add operations) is `LEDGER BAD` at 0 and 10 and `LEDGER ok` at 40 and 80, with the same lost store (printed-C: `mismatch` in all four). Counted with the temporary print: **90 distinct functions of hwram007 and 228 of hwram008** hit the cap in a whole-suite run (of 1,730 and 2,995 entries decompiled with lending: 5% and 8%; at most 11% and 15% of `TestGameCode`'s 839 and 1,554, whose functions are inside those), so "0 frame writes lost" holds for the rest only (A3-133, P2). The other hiding place I looked for, a value forwarded in an equal form to a reader that dies later, I did not build a loss for. Not found is not shown absent.

### 5. A3-127's class: piece and collapse arithmetic

`frame15.py` with one slot and the stores at every legal offset and width (bytes at 1 to 3 inside words, halfwords at 2, words), up to 24 stores, 1,600 call-free fixtures through the printed-C differential (700 filled by words, bytes or halves, 600 tiled with no fill (`cover`), 300 of every fill including none and save):

- **A3-131**: 3 of 600 tiled fixtures and 1 of 700 filled ones (a fill by halfwords through the pointer: the fill is itself stores through the collapse, so the bytes had no direct write under them), all `upper-bits`: a returned word with its high piece taken from a stack input. Reduced to R15-12a. It is 0068's own change: reverting the one line (`bytesBefore` back to `bytesAfter`) in a local build makes R15-12a to 12e, 13d and 16b right (it brings A3-127 back: the fixer's mutation table has that revert failing pins A, B, C, E, F and H);

### 2. Patches 0067, 0069 and 0070 by value

* **0070** (`sign_extend`, `getConsumeLocal`). Read: the left shift of `sign_extend` is the same bits as before (`in << ((8 - sizein) * 8)` unsigned, then the signed right shift by a count taken modulo 64 as x86 does; a negative count `(sizeout - sizein) * 8` is the bits `& 63`); `sizein` or `sizeout` of 0 still shifts by 64 (undefined as it was; no caller passes it). `PIECE` with a low input as wide as the output: before, x86's shift by 64 made the low input consume 0 bits (`b = outc ^ (a << 0) = 0` with `a = outc`), now `b = outc`: more consumed, never less, and no SH-2 code has a `PIECE` with an 8-byte low input. `INT_LEFT` by a constant of 64 or more: `outc >> (sa & 63)` is the count x86 used, so the same mask for 64 to 127 and a larger one than needed for 64 itself. **By value**: `address.cc` and `op.cc` linked in their pre-0070 form (the reverse patch, `-O2` as the tree) beside the tree's, the corpora run with both: the printed texts of all 839 and 1,554 functions (`SE_GAME_OUT`, and the lent pass in the same directory) are identical, file by file (`diff -rq`: 0 and 0). No fold changed.
* **0069** (the first operand of a nested `&&` or `||` is parenthesized). The printer paths that print a block condition are `no_branch` (the first block only), `only_branch` at the top, and `comma_separate` (nested as a second operand, the test of a `while` or `for`); only the last sets `nested`, and there the first operand is inside its own parentheses whatever it is. Every control construct that prints a condition goes through them (`emitBlockIf`, the overflow form of `emitBlockWhileDo`, `emitBlockDoWhile`, `emitForLoop`). The vendored `printc.cc` has no ternary token (`grep` finds none), so the nestings are `&&`, `||` and `!` (`!` is only printed over a leaf or a non-flippable operator, with the precedence table's parentheses; De Morgan is done on the leaves by the flip). Family 89 (random AND/OR/NOT trees of compares with statements in the leaves, depth up to 7, compiled with short-circuit branches into an if, an if-else, an else-if chain, a `while`, a `do-while` and a loop body with break and continue): 15,000 functions, 0 `mismatch` (one `narrow-c`), up to four `&&`/`||` in one condition; family 90 (a loop test that is such a tree, an extra break, a second loop sharing the exit): 5,000, 0; family 82 of round 15 (the carry `||`s, the shape of A2-101): 3,000, all agree.
* **0067** (`RuleSignMod2nOpt2`, `ActionLateDoNothing`, `RuleThreeWayCompare`, `RuleShiftSub`). Held by the families that build them: 73 `signmod` 3,000 (agree or `narrow-c`), 78 `randprog` and 67 `divterm` 3,000 each, the control-flow families of round 15 (79 to 81, 85: 12,000 functions) and the new ones (section 3: no endless text, no missing loop); the in-situ checks 0 bad over the rules of the pool.
